Question: Prediction
Model:
BCSC v3 (Breast Cancer Surveillance Consortium 5- and 10-year risk)
[code and data retrieved (public download, no password needed), awaiting a licence determination] 
Interim: BCRAT / Gail model (absolute invasive breast cancer risk) (1989)
Architecture detail: Relative risks fitted by conditional logistic regression, applied to race-specific baseline hazards and integrated year by year over the age interval against competing all-cause mortality, which is what converts them into an absolute risk.
Core formula:
A(t₁,t₂) = Σₐ [h₁(a) / (h₁(a)+h₂(a))] · e^(−Λ(a)) · [1 − e^(−(h₁(a)+h₂(a)))]

  h₁(a)  breast-cancer hazard  = RR(a) × race-specific baseline
  h₂(a)  competing all-cause mortality hazard
  Λ(a)   cumulative hazard up to age a
  a      runs year by year from t₁ to t₂
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Concordance 0.58 (95% CI 0.56-0.60) for 5-year risk in the Nurses' Health Study. Calibration is the model's strength, not discrimination, expected/observed 0.94 (0.89-0.99) in the same validation
Runs on EHR data?: No, needs questionnaire or patient-reported items. Age at menarche, age at first live birth, number of first-degree relatives with breast cancer and number of prior biopsies, a reproductive and family history interview.
Developed on: not recorded yet
Reference: Gail, M. H., Brinton, L. A., Byar, D. P., Corle, D. K., Green, S. B., Schairer, C., & Mulvihill, J. J. (1989). Projecting individualized probabilities of developing breast cancer for white females who are being examined annually. Journal of the National Cancer Institute, 81(24), 1879-86. https://doi.org/10.1093/jnci/81.24.1879
Where the equation sits: Not a single printed equation. The relative-risk and baseline-hazard tables (SEER incidence, NCHS mortality) and the year-by-year competing-risk integration are as shipped in the CRAN package BCRA; the integration follows its absolute.risk.R.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against CRAN BCRA 4 cases via absolute.risk(); worst absolute difference 3.7e-07 percentage points
Where the equation came from: NCI DCEG BCRAT algorithm; relative-risk and baseline-hazard (SEER incidence + NCHS mortality) tables as shipped in the CRAN package BCRA, absolute-risk integration follows its absolute.risk.R
Citation: Gail MH et al. J Natl Cancer Inst. 1989; NCI DCEG BCRAT algorithm
Scope / caveats: Six published Asian-American subgroups collapsed to a single 'asian' stratum using Chinese SEER rates as proxy, a deliberate simplification, documented in the module. Do not use for a specific Asian subgroup without restoring its own hazard vector.

Question: Prediction
Model:
BCSC v2.0 (Tice 2015, adds benign breast disease and a ten-year horizon)
[source gated behind a download-request form; article not open access] 
Interim: BCSC breast density model (Tice 2008, the BCSC calculator's version 1.0, 5-year risk) (2008)
Architecture detail: Third-order polynomial baseline invasive-incidence and exponential non-breast-cancer mortality, both by race/ethnicity, combined by a year-by-year competing-risk recursion into a race-specific 5-year risk; that risk is then standardized to the BI-RADS-2 reference density using age- and race-specific adjustment factors, multiplied by the woman's own density category's relative hazard, and (if known) by simple family-history and breast-biopsy multipliers.
Core formula:
I(x,r) = a_r·x³+b_r·x²+c_r·x+d_r   (annual incidence, % )
  D(x,r) = n_r·e^(m_r·x)      (annual non-BC mortality, % )
  P(x,r): P(a,r)=1; P(x,r) = P(x-1,r) − I(x-1,r) − D(x-1,r)
  AR_r = Σ_{x=a}^{a+4} I(x,r)·P(x,r)              (race-specific 5y risk)

  risk = AR_r × adjustment[r,age_band] × density_RH[age<65][density]
         × family_history_mult (if known) × biopsy_mult (if known)
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Concordance statistic 0.66 (95% CI 0.65-0.67) in the validation sample; age-adjusted c-statistic 0.622 (Table 4 / Results, the paper's own reported figures)
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. Age, race/ethnicity and BI-RADS breast density are already structured fields at a screening mammography site; family history and biopsy history are commonly captured but sometimes unknown, in which case the model skips that multiplier rather than imputing an average (the paper's own rule).
Developed on: 1,095,484 women age 35 or older across 7 BCSC mammography registries, 14,766 invasive breast cancers over a median 5.3 years of follow-up. Baselines fitted to 1998-2002 SEER incidence and 2002 US Vital Statistics. Read directly from the PDF, 2026-08-17.
Reference: Tice, J. A., Cummings, S. R., Smith-Bindman, R., Ichikawa, L., Barlow, W. E., & Kerlikowske, K. (2008). Using Clinical Factors and Mammographic Breast Density to Estimate Breast Cancer Risk: Development and Validation of a New Predictive Model. Annals of Internal Medicine, 148(5), 337-347. https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-148-5-200803040-00004
Where the equation sits: Appendix Figure, "The Breast Cancer Surveillance Consortium breast density model algorithm" (NIH Public Access manuscript pages 9-10): I(x,r) and D(x,r) polynomial/exponential tables, the P(x,r) recursion, the density relative-hazard table, and the age/race density-adjustment table. The family-history and biopsy-history multipliers are stated in prose in the paragraph beneath that table, not in a numbered display.
How it was verified: There is no independent reference implementation to check this against, the BCSC's own SAS macro that deploys this exact algorithm is behind the same password-gated request as the 2015/2024 updates (see `blocker` below)
Where the equation came from: Every coefficient comes from the paper's own "Appendix Figure. The Breast Cancer Surveillance Consortium breast density model algorithm", a fully closed-form algorithm with no external source needed, unlike every other candidate considered for this cell.
Citation: Tice JA, Cummings SR, Smith-Bindman R, et al. Using Clinical Factors and Mammographic Breast Density to Estimate Breast Cancer Risk. Ann Intern Med. 2008;148(5):337-347

Question: Response
Model: LDL-lowering absolute benefit (DERIVED: CTT trial effect x a baseline risk)
Architecture detail: Not a fitted model. A published trial rate ratio raised to the LDL reduction and applied multiplicatively to a baseline absolute risk from another model, yielding absolute risk reduction and number needed to treat.
Core formula:
ARR = baseline_risk × ( 1 − RR^ΔLDL )

  NNT = 1 / ARR
  RR  = 0.78 per 1.0 mmol/L LDL-C reduction   (CTT 2010)
        0.90 for all-cause mortality
  baseline_risk comes from a separate, verified model
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): n/a - this model does not rank patients, so it has no AUC. Its discrimination is whatever the upstream risk model supplies (PREVENT 0.794/0.757, or SCORE2)
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. Takes another model's output plus an intended LDL reduction; no patient fields of its own.
Developed on: CTT 2010: 26 randomised trials, 169,138 participants, median follow-up 4.8-5.1 years
Reference: Cholesterol Treatment Trialists’ (CTT) Collaboration, Baigent, C., Blackwell, L., Emberson, J., Holland, L. E., Reith, C., Bhala, N., Peto, R., Barnes, E. H., Keech, A., Simes, J., & Collins, R. (2010). Efficacy and safety of more intensive lowering of LDL cholesterol: a meta-analysis of data from 170,000 participants in 26 randomised trials. Lancet (London, England), 376(9753), 1670-81. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(10)61350-5
Where the equation sits: There is no source paper for this model because it is not a published prediction model, it is a composition this project defined from two published quantities (a CTT 2010 rate ratio and a separately verified baseline risk). The rate ratio's location in CTT 2010 is the only paper citation that applies.
How it was verified: NOT VERIFIABLE BY COMPARISON, and deliberately not claimed to be
Where the equation came from: NOT a published prediction model. A composition of two published quantities: the CTT 2010 rate ratio per 1.0 mmol/L LDL-C reduction (major vascular events RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.76-0.80; all-cause mortality RR 0.90, 0.87-0.93, read verbatim from the abstract, PMID 21067804) applied to an untreated absolute risk supplied by a separate, verified model. ARR = baseline x (1 - RR^delta_LDL); NNT = 1/ARR.
Citation: Cholesterol Treatment Trialists' Collaboration. Lancet. 2010;376(9753):1670-1681
Scope / caveats: The horizon and endpoint are whatever the baseline risk model's were, this function takes the baseline risk as an argument rather than computing it, so that stays visible. Four assumptions travel with every result: constant proportional effect across baseline risk (which is what CTT reports), a ~5-year trial effect carried to a 10-year horizon, CTT's major-vascular-events endpoint approximating the baseline model's endpoint, and a confidence interval covering the trial effect only, not baseline uncertainty.

score = age_points(age, prior_stroke) + F + D + CHF + H + P + R

  age_points   >=85    75-84   65-74    <65
    no stroke    6       5       3        0
    prior stroke 9       7       7        8

  F female   D diabetes   CHF heart failure
  H hypertension   P proteinuria   R eGFR<45 or ESRD     (each 1 point)

Neither is an exotic biomarker; both are already covered by egfr and a coded urinalysis result in the target platform crosswalk.
Developed on: not recorded yet
Reference: Singer, D. E., Chang, Y., Borowsky, L. H., Fang, M. C., Pomernacki, N. K., Udaltsova, N., Reynolds, K., & Go, A. S. (2013). A new risk scheme to predict ischemic stroke and other thromboembolism in atrial fibrillation: the ATRIA study stroke risk score. How it was verified: RELABELED 2026-08-17 from checked to not_checked
Where the equation came from: Table 3, PMC3698792 (CC BY-NC). An additive integer point table, same architecture family as CHA2DS2-VASc, no missing constant, nothing to ask an author for. Question: Response
Model: Moore criteria, response to cisplatin-based chemotherapy, advanced/recurrent/metastatic cervical carcinoma (GOG)
Architecture detail: Count of five binary risk factors (race, performance status, disease site, prior radiosensitizer, recurrence timing), each independently significant on multivariable analysis and explicitly NOT weighted by its odds ratio; banded 0-1 / 2-3 / 4-5 and reported against a published three-cell lookup of response rate and median PFS/OS in a development and an external cohort.
Core formula:
count = number of 5 binary factors present (race, PS>0, pelvic site, prior
        radiosensitizer, recurrence <=1yr from diagnosis). NOT a weighted sum
  band  = low 0-1 | mid 2-3 | high 4-5
  output = that band's published response rate and median PFS/OS,
           development cohort AND external (GOG 149) validation cohort

No intercept exists for the underlying logistic model and none is needed:
the published deliverable is the count and its three-cell outcome table.
`risk` is None, this is a lookup, not a fitted probability.
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): n/a as a c-index - no AUC or concordance is reported. Evidence is calibration plus separation, in an EXTERNAL cohort: predicted/observed response 50.9/42.6% low, 29.0/29.4% mid, 13.5/14.3% high risk (GOG 149, n=280), with median OS 11.93 / 7.59 / 5.58 months. Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.624 internally
Runs on EHR data?: Partly, needs pathology, imaging or a send-out assay. Race, prior radiosensitizer, and the recurrence interval are routine registry/chart fields. Performance status needs a clinician assessment (charted on a flowsheet where recorded) and disease site (pelvic vs. distant vs. combined) needs a staging work-up read from imaging/pathology reports rather than a single coded field. Nothing is a questionnaire or a radiomics feature.
Developed on: GOG 110 + 169 + 179 pooled: 428 enrolled, 409 with response data, overall response 32% (95% CI 27-36%). External validation: GOG 149 (not used in development). Prospective validation: GOG 240, n=452.
Reference: Moore, D. H., Tian, C., Monk, B. J., Long, H. J., Omura, G. A., & Bloss, J. D. (2010). Prognostic factors for response to cisplatin-based chemotherapy in advanced cervical carcinoma: A Gynecologic Oncology Group study. Gynecologic Oncology, 116(1), 44-49. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ygyno.2009.09.006
Where the equation sits: Table 3, "Multivariate Analysis of Prognostic Factors of Treatment Response" (five odds ratios, kept for provenance and never computed from) and Table 4, "Validation of Prognostic Model" (the three-band lookup this model returns). The construction rule ("comparable weights and no interactions... a simple prognostic index... combining the number of risk factors") is in the Results text. Prospective validation numbers are in the Results text of PMC4896296, not a table.
How it was verified: Nothing to re-derive: the paper declines to weight the five factors, so the model is a count, and the parity question is whether the lookup reproduces Table 4 exactly rather than whether an equation reproduces a formula
Where the equation came from: doi:10.1016/j.ygyno.2009.09.006, read from PMC4470610 on 2026-08-14. Table 3 ("Multivariate Analysis of Prognostic Factors of Treatment Response") gives five adjusted odds ratios; the paper states outright that these are NOT used as weights ("the five risk factors identified conferred comparable weights and there were no interactions across them, a simple prognostic index was developed by combining the number of risk factors"), so the model is a count 0-5, banded low 0-1 / mid 2-3 / high 4-5. Table 4 ("Validation of Prognostic Model") gives estimated/observed response rate and median PFS/OS for each band in both the development cohort (GOG 110+169+179, n=428) and the external validation cohort (GOG 149), a complete numeric statement over the entire three-cell output space. Prospective validation as a tertiary endpoint of GOG 240 (n=452) is in Tewari et al, Clin Cancer Res 2015;21(3):579-588, PMC4896296, Results text: low-risk 57% response/21.8mo OS, high-risk 18.5% response/8.2mo OS (mid-risk is Fig. 1 only, not transcribed).
Citation: Gynecol Oncol. 2010;116(1):44-49
Scope / caveats: Advanced, recurrent, or metastatic cervical carcinoma STARTING cisplatin-based chemotherapy, the GOG 110/169/179/149 population. Answers whether this regimen is likely to produce a response, not overall survival in general and not response to primary chemoradiation for newly diagnosed, non-metastatic disease, which is a different clinical question this model was never fit to. ONE OF THE FIVE INPUTS IS RACE (Black vs. non-Black, per Table 3; the paper's own prose alternates between "Black" and "African-American" for the same variable). It is a cohort-specific association the authors themselves discuss without resolving between access-to-care and biological explanations, and it is reproduced here as published rather than omitted, on the same basis as pbcg_extended's African- ancestry term, see that entry's scope_note, which documents a race coefficient that FLIPS SIGN between two of its own sub-models, the standing reminder in this library that these terms are cohort-specific and not stable biological constants. The disease-site input collapses a three-level source variable (pelvic / distant / combined) onto the paper's own binary factor (pelvic vs. non-pelvic); the paper never states in prose which side "combined" (13.1% of the development cohort) falls on. This module reads the label literally and files combined as non-pelvic, and flags every case where that inference was used.

Question: Prognosis
Model: ARRM, annual recurrence risk model, cervical cancer after primary surgery (SCCAN)
Architecture detail: Multivariable Cox model on five surgical-pathology predictors, its coefficients weighted to a 0-100 integer points score, banded into five risk groups, each band reported with the derivation cohort's observed disease-free survival and conditional annual recurrence risk.
Core formula:
score = Σ points(level)   over histotype, diameter, grade, nodes, LVSI

  points = round(β × 100/5.231)          5.231 = Σ largest β per predictor
  band   = 0 | 1-25 | 26-50 | 51-75 | 76-100     zero is its own band
  output = that band's observed KM disease-free survival and its
           CONDITIONAL annual recurrence risk, years 1-5

No baseline survival and no probability: this returns a group statistic,
so `risk` is None by design.
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Harrell's C 0.735 (95% CI 0.713; 0.757); ten-fold cross-validated AUC 0.732
Runs on EHR data?: Partly, needs pathology, imaging or a send-out assay. Five fields from the surgical pathology report, histotype, maximal pathologic tumour diameter, grade, number of positive pelvic nodes, lymphovascular space invasion. All are standard synoptic-report elements where one exists, and all are post-operative, so none is available at the point where a treatment decision is being made.
Developed on: SCCAN (Surveillance in Cervical CANcer) consortium, 4,343 early-stage cervical cancer patients treated 2007-2016 at 20 centres on four continents; 528 recurrences
Reference: Cibula, D., Dostálek, L., Jarkovsky, J., Mom, C. H., Lopez, A., Falconer, H., Fagotti, A., Ayhan, A., Kim, S. H., Isla Ortiz, D., Klat, J., Obermair, A., Landoni, F., Rodriguez, J., Manchanda, R., Kosťun, J., dos Reis, R., Meydanli, M. M., Odetto, D., ... van Lonkhuijzen, L. R.C.W. (2021). The annual recurrence risk model for tailored surveillance strategy in patients with cervical cancer. European Journal of Cancer, 158, 111-122. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2021.09.008
Where the equation sits: Table 2, "Multivariable model for the risk of recurrence" — β column and "Risk points (max. 100)" column, all five predictors with reference levels named. The construction sentence is in Methods, Statistical analysis. The band → outcome grid is Fig. 3 (a graphic); the only textual statements of it are five DFS values in the Abstract/Discussion and seven annual-risk values in Results, ARRM.
How it was verified: Two halves, checked separately because they carry different evidential weight
Where the equation came from: doi:10.1016/j.ejca.2021.09.008, Table 2, fourteen levels across five predictors, each non-reference level carrying a β and an integer "Risk points (max. 100)" value, every reference level named. Read from PMC9406128 on 2026-08-14. The points column is additionally re-derived from the β column alone: the paper states "A risk score was derived from regression coefficients (β) of the final model, which were weighted to the maximum sum of 100 points" and never prints the constant, so the divisor is 100 / (1.741 + 1.556 + 0.457 + 0.939 + 0.538) = 100/5.231 = 19.1168, and all thirteen published point values reproduce under round(β × 19.1168) with no exceptions. The band → outcome half is NOT printed as a table: Fig. 3 is a graphic and only twelve values appear in prose. The shipped grid was re-derived by re-running the deployed calculator's own estimator over the 4,343-row cohort that calculator ships client-side; all twelve printed values reproduce, ten of them exactly.
Scope / caveats: Early-stage cervical cancer treated by PRIMARY SURGERY. All five inputs are surgical pathology, so this cannot be run before an operation and does not apply to patients treated with definitive chemoradiation, who never produce a specimen. Tumour diameter is the pathologic measurement, not the imaged one. Outcome is disease-free survival from the date of surgery, and the annual recurrence risk is CONDITIONAL, the year-3 figure is the risk for a patient already recurrence-free for two years, not a cumulative risk. Two predictors pool "not assessed" with "negative" (pelvic nodes, LVSI), so an incomplete work-up scores identically to a clean one and a missing field is silently optimistic. The implementation reproduces that pooling and flags it in `notes` every time it fires. The 76-100 band contains 13 patients, 12 of whom recurred; the paper stops its landmark analysis there at year three and so does this module.

Question: Prediction
Model: CRC-PRO (10-year colorectal cancer risk, Multi-Ethnic Cohort)
Architecture detail: Two sex-specific Cox models with different predictor sets, each with restricted cubic splines on five or seven continuous predictors; risk is 1 - S0^exp(Xb) at a fixed 10-year horizon.
Core formula:
risk(10y) = 1 − S₀^exp(Xβ)

  S₀   = 0.9901043  (women)
         0.9846654  (men)
  Xβ   separate models per sex with DIFFERENT predictor sets
  splines on age, education, pack-years, BMI, alcohol
         (+ red meat and activity in men)
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Cross-validated C-statistic 0.681 (men), 0.679 (women)
Runs on EHR data?: No, needs questionnaire or patient-reported items. Years of education, pack-years, drinks per day, and for men ounces of red meat and hours of activity per day. These are cohort-study questionnaire items; no health record holds them.
Developed on: Multi-Ethnic Cohort Study
Reference: Wells, B. J., Kattan, M. W., Cooper, G. S., Jackson, L., & Koroukian, S. (2014). Colorectal cancer predicted risk online (CRC-PRO) calculator using data from the multi-ethnic cohort study. Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine, 27(1), 42-55. https://doi.org/10.3122/jabfm.2014.01.130040
Where the equation sits: Table 5A 'Coefficients for the Model Predicting Colorectal Cancer in Men' and Table 5B, the same for women. NOTE: the baseline survival values this library uses (0.9901043 women, 0.9846654 men) are NOT in the paper, they come from the vendor's R source at ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/ColorectalCancer. The paper never states the risk equation 1 - S0^exp(Xb) either; it shows nomograms.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R, route 1
Where the equation came from: J Am Board Fam Med 2014;27(1):42-55, doi:10.3122/jabfm.2014.01.130040 (open access, PMC4219857) for the model specification; coefficients from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/ColorectalCancer. Two SEPARATE models by sex with different predictor sets (the paper: NSAIDs matter for women only, red meat and activity for men only). Cox form, risk = 1 - S0^exp(Xb), S0 = 0.9901043 women / 0.9846654 men at 10 years; restricted cubic splines on age, education, pack-years, BMI and alcohol in both, plus red meat and activity in men.
Citation: Wells BJ, Kattan MW, Cooper GS, Jackson L, Koroukian S. J Am Board Fam Med. 2014;27(1):42-55
Scope / caveats: Multi-Ethnic Cohort (Hawaiian, Japanese, Latino, White, Black; Black is the reference). Validated input ranges enforced: age 45-85, weight 75-350 lb, height 60-80 in, pack-years 0-50, alcohol 0-12 drinks/day, education 6-20 y, red meat 0-5 oz/day, activity 0-4 h/day. Weight and height are IMPERIAL; the spline knots assume the app's own conversion. Note QCancer-10 validates better externally but has no open source.

Question: Response
Model: Wang 2024 dynamic nomogram, pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer
Architecture detail: Binary logistic regression (rms::lrm), six predictors on 9 degrees of freedom. T and N stage entered as unordered factors, histology and MRI EMVI and total neoadjuvant therapy as indicators, CEA as a linear term. Presented in the paper as a points nomogram and deployed as a web calculator.
Core formula:
logit(P(pCR)) = -0.0131
  + N-stage term        (reference cN0: cN1 -0.4513, cN2 -0.6596)
  + T-stage term        (reference cT2: cT1 +1.3364, cT3 +0.5773, cT4 +0.0587)
  - 1.1061 * [pre-CRT MRI EMVI positive]
  + 0.7642 * [total neoadjuvant therapy given]
  - 1.4323 * [signet-ring cell / mucinous histology]
  - 0.0584 * pre-CRT CEA in ng/mL

P(pCR) = 1 / (1 + exp(-logit))

The intercept is in NO published source. T stage is NOT monotone and its reference is cT2.
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): C-index 0.73 (95% CI 0.70-0.75) in the training cohort with an average of 0.73 across internal cross-validation, and 0.78 (0.72-0.83) in the external validation cohort. The deployed fit prints C 0.737 and Brier 0.151.
Runs on EHR data?: Partly, needs pathology, imaging or a send-out assay. Pre-treatment staging bundle: clinical T and N from staging MRI, EMVI status which requires the MRI to be read for it specifically and is not universally reported, biopsy histology, serum CEA, and whether total neoadjuvant therapy was given.
Developed on: 1579 patients, Union Hospital (Fujian Medical University), training; external validation 246 patients at Zhangzhou Hospital. 350/1579 (22.2%) achieved pCR.
Reference: Wang, G., Li, J., Huang, Y., & Guo, Y. (2024). A dynamic nomogram for predicting pathologic complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer. Cancer Medicine, 13(11), e7251. https://doi.org/10.1002/cam4.7251
Where the equation sits: Table 4 ("Univariate and multivariate Logistic regression analysis associated with pCR in the training cohort (n = 1579)") holds the multivariable odds ratios. Results 3.3 ("Nomogram for pCR") holds the sentence "Final formula for the nomogram = 22.0 x Pre-CRT N stage + ... + 3.85 x Pre-CR CEA". Figure 3A is the nomogram. NONE of the three carries an intercept or a points-to-probability mapping, which is why the coefficients here come from the calculator's Model Summary tab instead.
How it was verified: No worked example is published and no source release exists, so parity was established against the authors' own deployed calculator, the same artifact the coefficients came from, which makes this a transcription-and-coding check rather than an independent confirmation of the science, and it should…
Where the equation came from: SPLIT ACROSS TWO ARTIFACTS, AND THE PAPER IS NOT THE COMPLETE ONE. Cancer Med 2024;13(11):e7251 (doi:10.1002/cam4.7251, open access at PMC11141331) establishes the model, the cohort and the predictor set: Table 4 prints univariable and multivariable odds ratios (labelled "HR"), and Results 3.3 prints the nomogram's points formula. Neither states an intercept, and the points-to-probability axis exists only as a drawn scale inside Figure 3A, so the article alone can rank patients and cannot state a probability. There is no supplement and no erratum. The ten coefficients implemented here, intercept included, were read on 2026-08-14 from the "Model Summary" tab of the authors' own calculator at https://pcrpredict.shinyapps.io/LARC2/, whose URL the article prints twice. The app is built with R's DynNom, which renders the fitted object with R's own print method; for the rms::lrm fit behind this nomogram that is the entire coefficient table. The captured printout is committed at tests/parity/reference/wang_larc_pcr_model_summary.txt and pinned by test_the_committed_model_summary_still_matches_our_coefficients.
Citation: Wang G, Li J, Huang Y, Guo Y. Cancer Med. 2024;13(11):e7251
Scope / caveats: Locally advanced rectal cancer, staged BEFORE chemoradiotherapy, in patients who complete nCRT and proceed to surgery. All six inputs are pre-CRT values; feeding post-treatment (yp) staging in is a different question. CEA is bounded to 0-24 ng/mL, the authors' own slider range and the paper's explicit ">= 24" floor, and values outside are refused rather than extrapolated. Development was two Chinese centres, so transportability to other populations is untested beyond that.

Question: Prognosis
Model: MSK rectal calculator (RFS + OS after CRT and surgery)
Architecture detail: Cox proportional hazards with restricted cubic splines on age and positive-node count; survival is S0(t)^exp(X*beta) at four published follow-up times.
Core formula:
P(T ≥ t) = S₀(t)^exp(Xβ)

  S₀(t) published only at t = 0, 60, 120, 180 months
  Xβ    restricted cubic splines on age and positive-node count
  RFS and OS use DIFFERENT ypT reference groups
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): C-index 0.70 (95% CI 0.65-0.76) RFS and 0.73 (0.65-0.80) OS, internal validation; 0.71 and 0.72 external
Runs on EHR data?: Partly, needs pathology, imaging or a send-out assay. Post-treatment pathology: ypT stage, node count, venous and perineural invasion.
Developed on: 710 patients, Memorial Sloan Kettering, 1998-2014; externally validated at Siteman Cancer Center
Reference: Weiser, M. R., Chou, J. F., Keshinro, A., Chapman, W. C., Bauer, P. S., Mutch, M. G., Parikh, P. J., Cercek, A., Saltz, L. B., Gollub, M. J., Romesser, P. B., Crane, C. H., Shia, J., Markowitz, A. J., Garcia-Aguilar, J., Gönen, M., & Colorectal Cancer Disease Management Team of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (2021). Development and Assessment of a Clinical Calculator for Estimating the Likelihood of Recurrence and Survival Among Patients With Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Treated With Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy, and Surgery. JAMA Network Open, 4(11), e2133457. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.33457
Where the equation sits: Supplement 1: the eTable 'Parameter Estimates for Cox Regression Models Predicting RFS and OS' holds the coefficients, and the eFigure 'Predictive Equations for Incomplete Responders for RFS and OS' holds the assembled linear predictors. Main text describes it under 'Development of Clinical Calculators'. Which of the two governs was itself a defect in this project, settled against MSK's live calculator in favour of the eFigure.
How it was verified: No worked example is published, so parity was established against MSK's own hosted deployment of this model (mskcc.org/nomograms/rectal/post-treatment, whose Supporting Publication block cites this exact paper)
Where the equation came from: JAMA Netw Open 2021;4(11):e2133457, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.33457, Supplement 1 eFigure, full Cox linear predictor and baseline survival S0(t) at 0/60/120/180 months for both RFS and OS endpoints. Question: Prediction
Model: Kunzmann points model (esophageal adenocarcinoma)
Architecture detail: Points model derived from a stepwise logistic regression, with each coefficient divided by the smallest one, so the integer points ARE the model rather than a lossy summary.
Core formula:
points = Σ round_to_half( βᵢ / 0.40 )      (0–15)

  over age, sex, BMI, smoking, oesophageal condition
  refer for screening if points ≥ 8
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUROC 0.80 (95% CI 0.77-0.82); 0.79 internally validated
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. Age, sex, BMI, coded smoking status and a coded oesophageal diagnosis.
Developed on: UK Biobank; 355,034 participants aged 50+, 220 oesophageal adenocarcinomas within 5 years
Reference: Kunzmann, A. T., Thrift, A. P., Cardwell, C. R., Lagergren, J., Xie, S., Johnston, B. T., Anderson, L. A., Busby, J., McMenamin, Ú. C., Spence, A. D., & Coleman, H. G. (2018). Model for Identifying Individuals at Risk for Esophageal Adenocarcinoma. Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology, 16(8), 1229-1236.e4. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cgh.2018.03.014
Where the equation sits: Table 2, "Risk factors associated with oEAC in a stepwise logistic regression and the points assigned for the points based model", one table holding BOTH the fitted regression and the points, not two. Results section "EAC risk-prediction model: points-based model". Points = coefficient / smallest coefficient, rounded to the nearest 0.5; the Methods state that smallest coefficient as 0.40 (BMI 25-<30) and work an example with it, while the Table 2 footnote says 0.41, only 0.40 reproduces all ten published points, and the ten rows jointly admit only d in (0.3958, 0.4046]. Points independently confirmed against the published Figure 2 nomogram, "Nomogram for assigning points (out of a total of 15)".
How it was verified: No worked patient is published and the full text is paywalled, so this was the last model blocked on paper access; the PDF was supplied 2026-08-06
Where the equation came from: Table 2 points-based model, age 0/1.5/2.5/3.5, male 4.0, BMI 0/1.0/1.5/2.5, smoking never/former/current 0/2.0/3.5, esophageal condition 1.5; total 0-15, screening referral at >=8. Points are the fitted coefficients divided by the smallest and rounded to nearest 0.5. The Methods state that smallest coefficient as 0.40 (BMI 25-<30) and work an example, "the coefficient for men was 1.64 and the smallest coefficient in the model was 0.40 ..., so men were assigned 4 points (1.64/0.40, then rounded to nearest 0.5)". The Table 2 footnote says 0.41 and is the outlier; only 0.40 reproduces all ten published points.
Citation: Kunzmann AT, Thrift AP, Cardwell CR, et al. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol.
Scope / caveats: ADENOCARCINOMA only, not squamous cell carcinoma, different disease, different risk factors. UK Biobank volunteers aged 50+ (NOT primary care, the module docstring said primary care until 2026-08-18; the abstract says "enrolled in the UK Biobank prospective cohort study", and its healthy-volunteer bias means the absolute 5-year risks do not transfer to a primary-care list).

Question: Response
Model: Chau index (survival under first-line palliative chemotherapy, advanced esophago-gastric cancer)
Architecture detail: Count of four binary poor-prognosis factors, each independently significant at 99% confidence in a multivariable Cox model and explicitly NOT weighted by its hazard ratio; banded 0 / 1-2 / 3-4 and reported against the derivation cohort's published median and one-year overall survival for that band.
Core formula:
count = number of 4 binary factors present. NOT a weighted sum
          PS >= 2 · liver metastases · peritoneal metastases · ALP >= 100 U/L
  band  = good 0 | moderate 1-2 | poor 3-4
  output = that band's published median OS and one-year survival
           11.8 / 7.4 / 4.1 months;  48.5% / 25.7% / 11%

No intercept and no baseline survival are published, and none is needed:
the deliverable is the count and its three-cell outcome lookup.
`risk` is None. A SEPARATE logistic model for tumour response (Table 4)
drops liver metastases and prints no intercept, so no response
probability is recoverable and none is offered.
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. All four are routine at the point of starting palliative chemotherapy. Alkaline phosphatase is a standard liver-panel analyte; liver and peritoneal metastases are staging findings coded in the registry and stated in restaging imaging reports; performance status is charted on a flowsheet where a service records it. Nothing is a questionnaire, an imaging-derived feature or a specialist assay, the lightest input set of any response-axis model in this library.
Developed on: Pooled individual patient data from three randomised controlled trials at the Royal Marsden, 1992-2001: ECF v FAMTX (n=256), ECF v MCF (n=574), PVI FU v PVI FU+MMC (n=250). 1,080 patients, 979 (91%) died; the prognostic model is fitted on the 817 with complete data on all four factors.
Reference: Chau, I., Norman, A. R., Cunningham, D., Waters, J. S., Oates, J., & Ross, P. J. (2004). Multivariate prognostic factor analysis in locally advanced and metastatic esophago-gastric cancer, pooled analysis from three multicenter, randomized, controlled trials using individual patient data. Journal of Clinical Oncology, 22(12), 2395-2403. https://doi.org/10.1200/jco.2004.08.154
Where the equation sits: Table 3, "Multivariate Baseline Prognostic Model", holds the four hazard ratios with 99% CIs. Table 4, "Multivariate Logistic Regression Model for Tumor Response to Chemotherapy", is a DIFFERENT model and is recorded for provenance only. The risk-group definitions and every survival figure are in the Results PROSE under "Prognostic index", not in any table, which is why a reader scanning the tables alone will not find them. Baseline characteristics including the site-of-primary and histology breakdown are Table 1.
How it was verified: RELABELED 2026-08-17: parity_status was "checked", but no independent second source exists to check against, the article is CLOSED ACCESS with no repository copy anywhere, so tests/parity/test_chau_eg_parity.py compares the module's transcribed constants against a second hand-typed copy of the…
Where the equation came from: doi:10.1200/jco.2004.08.154, PMID 15197201, read in full on 2026-08-17. Table 3, "Multivariate Baseline Prognostic Model" (n=817 with complete data): performance status 2-3 HR 1.575 (99% CI 1.251-1.981), liver metastases 1.409 (1.139-1.743), peritoneal metastases 1.329 (1.013-1.743), alkaline phosphatase >=100 U/L 1.412 (1.136-1.755). The paper does NOT weight them, "All four factors have a similar order of magnitude, therefore they can be combined into a simple prognostic score without loss of relevant information", so the model is a count 0-4, banded good (0) / moderate (1-2) / poor (3-4). Risk-group outcomes are in the Results PROSE, not in any table: n = 239 / 487 / 91; median OS 11.8 / 7.4 / 4.1 months; one-year survival 48.5% (95% CI 41.9-54.7), 25.7% (22.5-29.7), 11% (5.6-18.4); HR versus good risk 1.92 (99% CI 1.53-2.40) and 3.59 (2.57-5.02). NOTE the abstract rounds Table 3 to 1.58 / 1.41 / 1.33 / 1.41. The table is primary and is what is stored; a reader working from the abstract is working from rounded values.
Scope / caveats: Locally advanced or metastatic esophago-gastric cancer at the START of first-line fluorouracil-based palliative chemotherapy. Answers how long this patient is likely to survive on that treatment, for deciding intensity and for trial stratification, not whether the tumour will shrink, and not anything about resectable disease. WHY AN "ESOPHAGO-GASTRIC" MODEL SITS IN AN ESOPHAGEAL CELL, since that is the obvious objection. Site of primary was esophagus 295 (27.3%), EGJ 248 (23.0%), stomach 512 (47.4%), unknown 25, so half the cohort (543, 50.3%) was esophageal or junctional. More importantly the authors tested site and found it did not matter: "Age, sex, and location of primary tumor were not significant in univariate analyses", and in the Discussion, "In our analysis, there were no survival differences among patients with esophageal, EGJ, or gastric cancers... there is no definite need for future phase III studies to distinguish patients with tumors from different anatomic origins if they have advanced disease." Contrast AGAMENON (Br J Cancer 2017), which also says "oesophagogastric" and is 5.8% esophagus against 83.9% stomach, the label is not evidence about a cohort, the site table is. TWO LIMITS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE SITE MIX. (1) Histology was 88% adenocarcinoma and 4.6% squamous, so this is NOT a model for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, the dominant histology across East Asia; applying it there is the same category error as running kunzmann on squamous disease. (2) The treatment era is 1992-2001 fluorouracil-based combination chemotherapy, predating trastuzumab and predating checkpoint inhibitors entirely. The authors state the index "requires validation" and name their own then-ongoing REAL-2 study as the intended validation set. No completed external validation is claimed by the paper, and none is claimed here.

Question: Prognosis
Model: Shapiro nomogram (overall survival after nCRT plus surgery, oesophageal/junctional cancer)
Architecture detail: Three-predictor nomogram from a multivariable Cox model, published as integer point scales (0-16 total) with the points-to-survival step printed numerically as labelled axes for 1-year and 5-year overall survival.
Core formula:
total = points(cN) + points(ypT) + points(ypN)          0-16
          cN0 0 · cN1 2
          ypT0 0 · ypT1 2 · ypT2 2 · ypT3 4
          ypN0 0 · ypN1 4 · ypN2 5 · ypN3 10

  survival = Fig. 1's printed axes, looked up at the total
          points  0  2  4  6  8 10 12 14 16
          1-year 91 88 85 81 75 68 60 51 41
          5-year 70 62 53 43 33 23 14  7  3

Totals 5, 7, 9 and 11 are reachable (every ypN2 patient) and are NOT
labelled; both survival figures return None there rather than an
interpolated value. `risk` is None, these are published percentages
for a points total, not a fitted individual probability.
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): c-index 0.63 at internal validation (0.62 and 0.63 on cross-validation between the two centres); 0.61 for OS and 0.64 for PFS on external validation in 975 patients
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. All three are cancer-registry staging fields already mapped in the crosswalk, the lightest input set of any model in this library. The trap is not availability but EDITION: cN must be UICC TNM 6th edition and binary, while ypT and ypN are 7th edition, and a warehouse that stores 8th-edition categories (or a modern three-level cN) is storing something this model was not fitted on.
Developed on: 626 of 661 screened patients treated with CROSS-regimen neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy plus resection at Erasmus MC Rotterdam and AMC Amsterdam (CROSS-I, CROSS-II and post-CROSS 2009-2013); adenocarcinoma 481 (76.8%), squamous 139 (22.2%)
Reference: Shapiro, J., van Klaveren, D., Lagarde, S. M., Toxopeus, E. L. A., van der Gaast, A., Hulshof, M. C. C. M., Wijnhoven, B. P. L., van Berge Henegouwen, M. I., Steyerberg, E. W., & van Lanschot, J. J. B. (2016). Prediction of survival in patients with oesophageal or junctional cancer receiving neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and surgery. British Journal of Surgery, 103(8), 1039-1047. https://doi.org/10.1002/bjs.10142
Where the equation sits: Fig. 1, "Nomogram for overall survival as developed in 626 patients", page 1043, the entire model, three predictor point scales plus a total-points axis and two survival axes whose ticks are LABELLED WITH NUMBERS rather than only drawn. The worked example is in Results, "Prediction model for survival". Table 1 holds the cohort and staging distributions. Table 2 is the FULL multivariable model and is NOT the fitted nomogram, its hazard ratios do not reproduce the points, and the final model's coefficients are printed nowhere in the article.
How it was verified: No fixture and no reference script: the model is three integer scales and a printed lookup, so parity means whether every transcribed constant equals the figure
Where the equation came from: doi:10.1002/bjs.10142, PMID 27115731, read in full on 2026-08-17. Fig. 1 is the whole model. Three predictor scales: cN0 0 / cN1 2; ypT0 0 / ypT1 2 / ypT2 2 / ypT3 4; ypN0 0 / ypN1 4 / ypN2 5 / ypN3 10, total 0-16. Then, and this is what makes the paper usable where four cervical nomogram papers were not, the points-to-probability step is printed NUMERICALLY rather than drawn: the total-points axis carries ticks at 0 2 4 6 8 10 12 14 16 with 1-year survival 91 88 85 81 75 68 60 51 41 and 5-year survival 70 62 53 43 33 23 14 7 3 beneath them. Read from pdftotext -layout and independently confirmed against PNG renders of page 1043 at 300 and 600 dpi. The worked example in the Results reproduces exactly: cN1 with a complete response (ypT0, ypN0) totals 2 points for "estimated 1- and 5-year survival rates of 88 and 62 per cent respectively". NOT USABLE FROM THIS PAPER: the final model's Cox coefficients, which are printed nowhere -- Table 2 is the FULL multivariable model and its hazard ratios do not reproduce these points.
Scope / caveats: Oesophageal or oesophagogastric junctional carcinoma treated with CROSS-regimen neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy FOLLOWED BY RESECTION. Two of the three inputs are post-resection pathology, so this cannot be run pre-operatively and says nothing about whether to operate, which is the question someone reaching for an "oesophageal prognosis model" most often has. FOUR OF THIRTEEN REACHABLE SCORES HAVE NO PUBLISHED SURVIVAL, and the module returns None for them rather than interpolating. Fig. 1 labels even totals only; ypN2 scores 5 and is the model's only odd point value, so every ypN2 patient (3-6 positive nodes, 60 of 626 = 9.6% of the derivation cohort) lands between labelled ticks. A Cox fit reproduces the printed axis to 0.36 percentage points and would fill the gap convincingly, which is precisely why it is not used. DISCRIMINATION IS WEAK and should be quoted whenever the model is: c-index 0.63 at internal validation, 0.62/0.63 on cross-validation between the two centres, 0.61 on external validation. The authors say so themselves, predicted survival showed "only moderate correlation with observed survival, emphasizing the need for new prognostic factors". Squamous histology is well represented here (139 of 626, 22.2%) unlike chau_eg (4.6%), so the two esophageal models differ in applicability by histology and the chau_eg caveat must not be carried across. Staging editions are mixed and are not interchangeable: cN is UICC TNM SIXTH edition and binary (cN0/cN1 only, not the modern N0-N3), while ypT and ypN are seventh edition. Feeding eighth-edition categories or a three-level cN is feeding the model something it was never fitted on; the module refuses rather than mis-scoring.

Question: Prediction
Model: ABC method (H. pylori antibody x pepsinogen serological groups A-D)
Architecture detail: A 2x2 cross-tabulation, not a regression: H. pylori serology (+/-) crossed with pepsinogen-defined atrophy (+/-) gives 4 ordered groups A-D.
Core formula:
group = H. pylori antibody (±)  ×  pepsinogen atrophy (±)

  atrophy = PG I ≤ 70 ng/mL  AND  PG I / PG II ≤ 3.0
  → groups A, B, C, D, each with a published annual incidence
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): n/a as a c-index - the paper reports no AUC or concordance. Evidence is stratification: annual gastric-cancer incidence 0.04 / 0.06 / 0.35 / 0.60 %/y for groups A / B / C / D (log-rank p<0.0001), with Cox hazard ratios vs A of 1.1 (0.4-3.4, p=0.81), 6.0 (2.4-14.5), 8.2 (3.2-21.5). GROUP B IS NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM A
Runs on EHR data?: Partly, needs pathology, imaging or a send-out assay. Pepsinogen I and the I/II ratio with H. pylori serology. Routine screening in Japan, rarely ordered elsewhere.
Developed on: not recorded yet
Reference: Watabe, H., Mitsushima, T., Yamaji, Y., Okamoto, M., Wada, R., Kokubo, T., Doi, H., Yoshida, H., Kawabe, T., & Omata, M. (2005). Predicting the development of gastric cancer from combining Helicobacter pylori antibodies and serum pepsinogen status: a prospective endoscopic cohort study. Gut, 54(6), 764-8. https://doi.org/10.1136/gut.2004.055400
Where the equation sits: Methods, subsection 'Serum pepsinogen level' defines atrophy (PG I <=70 ng/mL AND PG I/II <=3.0); Methods, subsection 'Classification by anti-H pylori antibody and serum pepsinogen status' defines groups A-D; the per-group annual incidence rates are in Table 2.
How it was verified: Route 5: incidence rates re-derived independently from the paper's own cases and person-years (Tables 1-2): 7/(3324*4.8y)=0.044%/y, 6/(2134*4.7y)=0.060%/y, 18/(1082*4.7y)=0.354%/y, 12/(443*4.5y)=0.602%/y, each reproduces the published rate
Where the equation came from: Gut 2005;54(6):764-768, doi:10.1136/gut.2004.055400, PMC1774550, group rule from Table 1/Methods (PG+ <=> PG I <=70 ng/mL AND PG I/II <=3.0), annual incidence from Table 2
Citation: Watabe H et al. Gut. 2005;54(6):764-768
Scope / caveats: Japanese cohort absolute rates; ordering transfers, absolute numbers do not. Invalid after H. pylori eradication (seroreversion).

Question: Response
Model: Integer risk score for complete tumour regression (Ryan TRG 0) after preoperative chemotherapy in advanced gastric cancer
Architecture detail: Four dichotomised pretreatment values with integer weights (5, 4, 7, 7) summed to 0-23, split at 13. A logistic regression derives the weights and is then not used again, so the score is the model.
Core formula:
score = 5·[CA19-9 ≤ 10.90 U/mL] + 4·[CA72-4 ≤ 3.19 U/mL]
        + 7·[well differentiated] + 7·[LNmax ≥ 1.535 cm]

  range 0–23; high risk if score > 13

  observed pCR: 0% at ≤13 points, 22.35% above
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUC 0.84 (0.77–0.91) training, 0.73 (0.55–0.91) internal validation, 0.82 (0.71–0.92) prospective cohort. No C-index and no calibration analysis are reported anywhere in the paper.
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. CA19-9 and CA72-4 are routine serum tumour markers, differentiation grade comes from the diagnostic biopsy report, and LNmax is a short-axis node measurement already made on the staging MDCT. CA72-4 is ordered less widely outside East Asia than the other three.
Developed on: 428 patients at Shanghai Ruijin Hospital, 304 retrospective (July 2009–November 2018), split 2:1 at random into 202 training and 102 internal validation, plus 124 enrolled prospectively December 2018–June 2020 after the model was locked
Reference: Xu, W., Ma, Q., Wang, L., He, C., Lu, S., Ni, Z., Hua, Z., Zhu, Z., Yang, Z., Zheng, Y., Feng, R., Yan, C., Li, C., Yao, X., Chen, M., Liu, W., Yan, M., & Zhu, Z. (2021). Prediction Model of Tumor Regression Grade for Advanced Gastric Cancer After Preoperative Chemotherapy. Frontiers in Oncology, 11, 607640. https://doi.org/10.3389/fonc.2021.607640
Where the equation sits: Table 4, "Risk Score of Prediction Model for TRG", the four point assignments. The betas behind them are Table 3, "Multivariate analysis: variables correlated with TRG in the training set". Both are real HTML tables in PMC8082104, so no figure has to be read.
How it was verified: RELABELED 2026-08-17 from a "checked" that its own text already contradicted: this entry said "CHECKED" while stating in the very next sentence "this is not a parity run against an independent implementation and is not claimed as one", caught by an audit that treats a checked/matched status paired…
Where the equation came from: Table 4 "Risk Score of Prediction Model for TRG" gives the four point values (CA19-9 <=10.90 U/mL 5, CA72-4 <=3.19 U/mL 4, well differentiation 7, LNmax >=1.535 cm 7). Table 3 "Multivariate analysis: variables correlated with TRG in the training set" gives the coefficients behind them (B 1.725, 1.511, 2.005, 2.073; OR 5.615, 4.531, 7.426, 7.945). The 0-23 range, the 13-point cut-off and the three cut-off values are in the Results text. Both tables are machine-readable in PMC8082104 and the paper contains no nomogram figure, so nothing was read off an image.
Citation: Xu W, Ma Q, Wang L, et al. Front Oncol. 2021;11:607640
Scope / caveats: Locally advanced gastric adenocarcinoma receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Endpoint is Ryan TRG 0, i.e. pathological complete response, at resection. Three limits that belong next to any number this produces. First, it is single-centre: the paper calls its prospective cohort an "external validation group" but every author is at Shanghai Ruijin, only one hospital is ever named, and the paper's own limitations say "This was a single-center clinical study". It is prospective TEMPORAL validation. Second, it is thin, 30 TRG=0 events in the retrospective data, 20 of them in training against four retained predictors, so events per variable is about 5 and the 0.84 is optimistic on its face; the internal AUC rests on 10 events with a CI running down to 0.55, and the prospective AUC on 9. Third, it outputs a risk group, not a probability, and no calibration was ever assessed. The temporal validation is worth more than it first looks. Regimens changed between the eras (EOX and taxane-containing retrospectively, SOX and FLOT prospectively), so it is a genuine out-of-era test, which matters, because PMID 35280802 showed a gastric response signature holding at AUC 0.72–0.78 across chemotherapy regimens and collapsing to 0.50 under apatinib + SOX.

Question: Prognosis
Model: MSK gastric nomogram (disease-specific survival after R0 resection)
Architecture detail: Cox proportional hazards with restricted cubic splines on age, positive nodes, negative nodes and depth of invasion; depth is an ordinal 1-7 entered as a continuous splined term, not as indicators.
Core formula:
DSS(t) = S₀(t)^exp(Xβ)

  S₀ = 0.579053   at 5 years
       0.5089101  at 9 years
  Xβ   splines on age, positive nodes, negative nodes, depth
  references: female, Lauren diffuse, antrum/pyloric
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Concordance index 0.80, bootstrap-corrected
Runs on EHR data?: Partly, needs pathology, imaging or a send-out assay. Staging and pathology detail: Lauren type, depth of invasion, and counts of positive AND negative nodes, the negative count is often missing even where the positive one is recorded.
Developed on: Memorial Sloan Kettering gastric resection series
Reference: Kattan, M. W., Karpeh, M. S., Mazumdar, M., & Brennan, M. F. (2003). Postoperative nomogram for disease-specific survival after an R0 resection for gastric carcinoma. Journal of Clinical Oncology, 21(19), 3647-50. https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2003.01.240
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form: J Clin Oncol 2003;21(19) prints a nomogram figure only. Coefficients from ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/GastricCancer (server.R), with S0 at 5 years (0.579053) and 9 years (0.5089101).
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R, route 1
Where the equation came from: NOT the paper: J Clin Oncol 2003;21(19) publishes a nomogram figure and no closed-form model. The coefficients come from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/GastricCancer (server.R), which riskcalc.org's own page cites to Kattan 2003. Cox form DSS(t) = S0(t)^exp(Xb) with S0 published at 5 years (0.579053) and 9 years (0.5089101); restricted cubic splines on age, positive nodes, negative nodes and depth.
Citation: Kattan MW, Karpeh MS, Mazumdar M, Brennan MF. J Clin Oncol. 2003;21(19):3647-3650
Scope / caveats: Patients after R0 resection for gastric carcinoma. The hosted calculator validates age 25-96, positive nodes 0-23, negative nodes 0-146, size 0.1-21 cm; those bounds are enforced because the splines are only anchored inside them.

Question: Prediction
Model: UK Biobank head and neck cancer risk model (7-year absolute risk)
Architecture detail: Single logistic regression on eight predictors, two continuous and six categorical, with the constant published in the coefficient table's caption.
Core formula:
logit(p) = -9.54
         + ln(1.04) * age        (per year, uncentred)
         + ln(0.96) * BMI        (per unit, PROTECTIVE)
         + ln(1.81) * male

         + smoking    never 0 | previous ln(1.59) | current ln(3.10)
         + Townsend   Q1 0 | Q2 ln(1.30) | Q3 ln(1.14) | Q4 ln(1.81) | Q5 ln(1.66)
         + alcohol    never 0 | previous ln(3.26) | current ln(1.42)
         + exercise   none 0 | 1-4 d ln(0.68) | >=5 d ln(0.66)
         + fruit/veg  <5/day 0 | >=5/day ln(0.71)

  p = 7-year risk of ICD-10 C00-C14 or C30-C31   (larynx C32 EXCLUDED)
  Q4 > Q5 and previous > current alcohol are in the paper, not typos.
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): C-statistic 0.69 (95% CI 0.66-0.71) in development with good calibration; 0.64 (0.60-0.68) on the North West subset with reasonable calibration
Runs on EHR data?: No, needs questionnaire or patient-reported items. Age, sex, BMI and coded smoking are routine. Three inputs are not. The Townsend Deprivation Index is a UK AREA-LEVEL measure with no US equivalent, the same class of problem recorded for PREVENT's SDI decile, where the closest thing on the target platform platform is a differently-scaled Vizient vulnerability index. Moderate-exercise days per week and five-a-day fruit and vegetable intake are questionnaire items. That is three of eight predictors with no routine source, which is why this is not_ehr rather than routine, matching crc_pro.
Developed on: UK Biobank, 502,647 recruited aged 40-69; model fitted on 397,179 complete cases with 232 incident head and neck cancers in the 7 years after recruitment
Reference: Mccarthy, C. E., Bonnet, L. J., Marcus, M. W., & Field, J. K. (2020). Development and validation of a multivariable risk prediction model for head and neck cancer using the UK Biobank. International Journal of Oncology, 57(5), 1192-1202. https://doi.org/10.3892/ijo.2020.5123
Where the equation sits: Table III, 'Multivariable model for head and neck cancer risk in the UK Biobank'. Odds ratios with reference levels in the body; the model intercept in the caption, together with the complete-case count (397,179 observations, 232 cases, 396,947 controls).
How it was verified: TRANSCRIPTION CHECKED 2026-08-17 against Table III, every cell, and RE-CHECKED 2026-08-18 against a second, open-access copy of the same table (see equation_source), still NOT parity in the sense this registry uses the word, and still labelled not_checked deliberately, because both checks confirm…
Where the equation came from: Table III of the article, read on 2026-08-17. The eight odds ratios are in the table body and THE INTERCEPT IS IN THE CAPTION, "Model Intercept Coefficient -9.54 (95% confidence interval, -11.2 - -7.88; P<0.001)", which is the whole reason this cell could be closed. Three earlier passes over this literature recorded head and neck detection as having no implementable model; two of them never saw this paper, and the third saw it and could not open it. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-18 against a second, openly-accessible copy: the University of Liverpool institutional repository hosts the author-accepted manuscript free of charge at https://livrepository.liverpool.ac.uk/3109887/ ("Final IJO manuscript_word.docx"). Every one of the eight odds ratios, all four Townsend quintile terms, and the intercept with its 95% CI were re-extracted from that .docx independently of the original PDF-based transcription, all values agree exactly, character for character. This matters beyond redundancy: this copy is openly accessible, so it is now the recommended re-verification route.
Citation: McCarthy CE, Bonnet LJ, Marcus MW, Field JK. Development and validation of a multivariable risk prediction model for head and neck cancer using the UK Biobank. Int J Oncol. 2020;57(5):1192-1202
Scope / caveats: Incident ICD-10 C00-C14 and C30-C31 within 7 years of a baseline assessment. LARYNGEAL CANCER (C32) IS EXCLUDED from the outcome by design, the authors dropped it because "screening for oral cancers and laryngeal cancers requires different expertise and laryngeal cancer would not be visible during routine oral examination". A caller who wants all head and neck sites is asking a different question. UK population, 40-69 at entry.

Question: Prognosis
Model: Ang 2010 RPA risk groups (HPV / smoking / stage, oropharynx)
Architecture detail: Recursive-partitioning (CART) decision tree: three binary splits on HPV status, pack-years and nodal/tumour stage produce 3 risk groups.
Core formula:
HPV+ ─┬─ ≤10 pack-years ─────────────→ low
      └─ >10 ─┬─ N0–N2a ────────────→ low
              └─ N2b–N3 ───────────→ intermediate

HPV− ─┬─ ≤10 pack-years, T2–T3 ────→ intermediate
      └─ otherwise ────────────────→ high
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): n/a as a c-index - no AUC or concordance is reported. Evidence is separation: 3-year overall survival 93.0% (95% CI 88.3-97.7) low risk, 70.8% (60.7-80.8) intermediate, 46.2% (34.7-57.7) high, with hazard ratios vs low of 3.54 and 7.16. Non-overlapping confidence intervals across all three groups
Runs on EHR data?: No, needs questionnaire or patient-reported items. HPV status and stage are specialty data, but the rule turns on a pack-years threshold, and pack-years as a number is rarely recorded.
Developed on: not recorded yet
Reference: Ang, K. K., Harris, J., Wheeler, R., Weber, R., Rosenthal, D. I., Nguyen-Tân, P. F., Westra, W. H., Chung, C. H., Jordan, R. C., Lu, C., Kim, H., Axelrod, R., Silverman, C. C., Redmond, K. P., & Gillison, M. L. (2010). Human papillomavirus and survival of patients with oropharyngeal cancer. The New England Journal of Medicine, 363(1), 24-35. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0912217
Where the equation sits: Results, subsection 'HPV status and survival', stated as prose and drawn as the recursive-partitioning tree in Figure 2. No table.
How it was verified: RELABELED 2026-08-17: this used to say Fakhry et al
Where the equation came from: PMC2943767, verbatim Results-section quote. HPV-positive: low risk except smokers (>10 pack-years) with N2b-N3 = intermediate; HPV-negative: high risk except nonsmokers with T2/T3 = intermediate
Citation: Ang KK et al. N Engl J Med. 2010;363(1):24-35 (RTOG 0129)
Scope / caveats: Known ambiguity, documented in code: the primary text uses '>10 pack-years' for the HPV-positive branch's smoking split but 'nonsmokers' (undefined precisely) for the HPV-negative branch's exception. We apply the same <=10/>10 pack-years split to both branches as the more defensible reading; flagged, not silently resolved.

Question: Prediction
Model: aMAP score (5-year HCC risk in chronic hepatitis)
Architecture detail: Linear score on age, sex, ALBI and platelets, rescaled onto 0-100 and banded at 50 and 60; it embeds the whole ALBI score as one term.
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): C-index 0.82–0.87 across aetiologies and ethnicities
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. Age, sex, platelets, bilirubin, albumin, a CBC and a liver panel.
Developed on: 11 global prospective cohorts, 17,374 patients with chronic hepatitis
Reference: Fan, R., Papatheodoridis, G., Sun, J., Innes, H., Toyoda, H., Xie, Q., Mo, S., Sypsa, V., Guha, I. N., Kumada, T., Niu, J., Dalekos, G., Yasuda, S., Barnes, E., Lian, J., Suri, V., Idilman, R., Barclay, S. T., Dou, X., . . . Hou, J. (2020). aMAP risk score predicts hepatocellular carcinoma development in patients with chronic hepatitis. Journal of Hepatology, 73(6), 1368-1378. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhep.2020.07.025
Where the equation sits: The formula is a display equation in prose, not a table and not a figure, in Results, "Derivation of the HCC risk score", introduced by "A risk score, known as the age-male-ALBI-platelets (aMAP) score, was devised using the above 4 variables weighted by their regression coefficients in the multivariable Cox model (Table 2), and then the score range was standardised to 1-100". The 5-year baseline survival S0(t) = exp(-H0(t)) = 0.984 is stated immediately after it. The ALBI sub-formula has its own locus: Methods, "Albumin-bilirubin score calculation". The 50 and 60 cut-offs are in Results, "HCC risk stratification based on the aMAP score", "The X-tile plots were used to generate 2 optimal cut-off values (50 and 60)", derived in Figure S4 and named again in the caption of Table 4. TWO THINGS THIS RE-READ CORRECTED. First, the range: the Results body says "standardised to 1-100", not 0-100. The paper contradicts itself, the abstract's Results says the score ranges "from 0 to 100" and the lay summary repeats it, so the 0-100 reading is the one most readers will meet. Take the Results body sentence as primary, since it is the one attached to the formula. Second, and more useful: the published formula uses ROUNDED coefficients. Table 2, "Cox regression analysis in the training cohort.", multivariable Coefficient column, gives age 0.060, male sex 0.894, ALBI 0.484, platelets -0.012, while the formula prints 0.06 / 0.89 / 0.48 / -0.01. That is a real reproducibility fork, implementing from Table 2 gives different scores from implementing the formula. We implement the formula, deliberately: it is what the 50/60 cut-offs were calibrated against and what the deployed calculator computes.
How it was verified: No numeric worked example is published, so parity was established against the custodial calculator hosted by CUHK's Medical Data Analytics Centre, an aMAP collaborating site (mdac.cuhk.edu.hk/calculators/amap/)
Where the equation came from: J Hepatol 2020;73(6):1368-1378, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2020.07.025 (open access CC BY-NC-ND), aMAP = ({0.06*age + 0.89*male + 0.48*ALBI - 0.01*platelets} + 7.4)/14.77*100; ALBI = 0.66*log10(bilirubin umol/L) - 0.085*albumin g/L; cut-offs 50 and 60
Citation: Fan R, Papatheodoridis G, Sun J, et al. J Hepatol. 2020;73(6):1368-1378
Scope / caveats: -- this used to claim aMAP's -0.085 differed from "Johnson 2015's -0.0852", asserting the disproven -0.0852 reading as the paper's real value. Johnson 2015 itself prints -0.085 (see the albi entry's parity_note, confirmed against the primary text); -0.0852 was this project's own pre-2026-08-05 transcription error in the albi module, not a second published rounding. aMAP and ALBI use the identical -0.085 coefficient; there is no rounding difference between them to explain.

Question: Response
Model: HAP score (pre-TACE prognosis / candidacy)
Architecture detail: Additive integer point score (0-4) from 4 dichotomised variables, mapped to 4 prognostic grades.
Core formula:
points = [albumin < 36 g/L] + [bilirubin > 17 µmol/L]
       + [AFP > 400 ng/mL] + [dominant tumour > 7 cm]

  0 → grade A,  1 → B,  2 → C,  >2 → D
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUROC for mortality, HAP: 1-year 0.79 (95% CI 0.69-0.88) training, 0.67 (0.58-0.76) validation; 2-year 0.82 (0.73-0.92) training, 0.64 (0.49-0.78) validation. Highest of the six scores compared at both time points, but the validation advantage is significant only at 1 year (P=0.02); at 2 years P=0.71

Question: Prediction
Model: Optum EHR LASSO model (3-year lung cancer risk from routine care)
Architecture detail: LASSO (L1-penalised) logistic regression fitted with Cyclops over 16,633 candidate OMOP covariates; the penalty left 278 non-zero. Prediction is a plain dot product over covariateIds through a logistic link, no splines, no interactions, no per-patient normalisation, because every surviving covariate is a 0/1 indicator whose stored normalisation factor is 1.
Core formula:
p(lung cancer in days 1-1095) = 1 / (1 + e^(-XB))

  XB = -8.8024 + sum over the 278 covariates of beta_i * x_i
  x_i  = value of covariateId i, divided by its normFactor (all 1 here)
  covariateId = conceptId * 1000 + analysisId, observed in day -365..0
  a covariateId the model does not carry contributes nothing
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUC 0.76 internal; 0.81 on external validation in the Mercy EHR and 0.72 in Optum claims
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. Pure EHR: diagnoses, medications, laboratory results, procedures, visits, devices, demographics and coded smoking status. No questionnaire item anywhere, which is the point of carrying it next to PLCOm2012, whose pack-years, years-since-quitting and education level are survey fields an EHR does not hold. The caveat is the shape of the input, not its availability: the caller supplies OMOP covariateIds from a FeatureExtraction run, so a site that is not already on the OMOP CDM has an extraction to build before it has a prediction.
Developed on: 4,777,606 patients in Optum's de-identified EHR dataset (cdm_optum_ehr_v1705); external validation in the Mercy EHR and in Optum claims
Reference: Chandran, U., Reps, J., Yang, R., Vachani, A., Maldonado, F., & Kalsekar, I. (2023). Machine Learning and Real-World Data to Predict Lung Cancer Risk in Routine Care. Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 32(3), 337-343. https://doi.org/10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-22-0873
Where the equation sits: ohdsi-studies/lungCancerPrognostic at 61c526ea, inst/models/full_model/. model.json holds the intercept and 16,633 betas (279 non-zero including the intercept); covariateImportance.csv holds the same coefficients unrounded plus a covariateName, analysisId and conceptId for each; preprocessing.json holds the normFactors applied at predict time; trainDetails.json names cdm_optum_ehr_v1705 and the 4,777,606-patient attrition. The prediction function is PatientLevelPrediction's predictCyclopsType, in R/CyclopsModels.R.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-14, route 1, against PatientLevelPrediction 6.6.0 itself: the reference values come from loadPlpModel + predictPlp on the study package's own model directory, so the vendor's whole predict path runs, covariate deletion, normalisation by normFactors, the join on covariateId, the dot…
Top predictor: coded smoking status, then age band
Where the equation came from: The fitted model itself, not the paper: inst/models/full_model/model.json in the Apache-2.0 study package, which is the artifact PatientLevelPrediction loads and scores with. The paper prints no coefficient table, it reports AUCs and names the top predictors, so the package is the only complete statement of the equation, and it is a machine-readable one.
Citation: Chandran U, Reps J, Yang R, Vachani A, Maldonado F, Kalsekar I. Machine Learning and Real-World Data to Predict Lung Cancer Risk in Routine Care. Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev. 2023;32(3):337-343
Scope / caveats: Optum de-identified EHR (cdm_optum_ehr_v1705): patients aged 45-65 with a 2013 outpatient visit, at least 365 days of prior observation and no prior lung cancer; 4,777,606 patients and 3,661 outcomes. Predicts a FIRST lung cancer diagnosis in days 1-1095 after the index visit. Three things to know before pointing it at data. (1) The inputs are OMOP covariateIds, not clinical variables, so the caller must already be extracting FeatureExtraction covariates under the settings in modelDesign.json, a different lookback window makes the same id mean something else. (2) Absence and zero are indistinguishable: the covariate set was built with missingMeansZero, so an under-coded record scores like a healthy one, and this is the failure mode to watch in deployment rather than a miscalibrated coefficient. (3) The model learned one vendor's coding habits. Its fourth and fifth largest coefficients are a body-temperature measurement (-0.8444) and a temperature observation (+0.8025), the same clinical fact filed in two OMOP domains, with opposite signs. That is care-utilisation and documentation signal, not lung biology. It survived external validation (AUC 0.81 in the Mercy EHR) but that is not a guarantee for a third database.

Where the equation sits: Table 1, titled 'Enriching New-onset Diabetes for Pancreatic Cancer (END-PDAC) score parameters', note the table says END-PDAC, not END-PAC.
