How it was verified: RELABELED 2026-08-17: both routes used here check the implementation against the SAME primary source it was built from, not against anything independent, so "checked" overclaimed what was actually done, docs/VERIFICATION.md says as much already ("No external source was involved")
Where the equation came from: Gastroenterology 2018;155(3):730-739.e3, Table 1 (END-PAC score parameters), read from the NIH author manuscript. Three additive terms: blood-glucose CATEGORY difference (range 1-4), weight change over the preceding year (-6..+6, loss scores positive), age at diabetes onset (-1..+1). Total -6..11; >=3 high risk, <=0 extremely low risk. this field still read the pre-fix "<0" threshold after parity_note and core_formula were both corrected to "<=0" on 2026-08-06, three fields describing the one defect this project caught had drifted out of sync with each other.
Citation: Sharma A, Kandlakunta H, Nagpal SJS, et al. Gastroenterology. 2018;155(3):730-739.e3
Scope / caveats: Adults with glycemically-defined new-onset diabetes (validation in >=50-year-olds). Enriches an already-selected group; NOT a general-population screen.

Question: Prognosis
Model: MSK pancreatic nomogram (disease-specific survival after resection)
Architecture detail: Cox proportional hazards with restricted cubic splines on positive-node count and tumour size, plus ten categorical and binary terms; three published horizons.
Core formula:
S(t) = S₀(t)^exp(Xβ)

  S₀ = 0.6775     at 12 months
       0.3457804  at 24 months
       0.1976732  at 36 months
  Xβ   splines on positive-node count and tumour size, plus ten
       categorical and binary terms; T stage is non-monotone
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Bootstrap-corrected concordance index 0.64 internally (200 resamples, on the 555-patient MSK development cohort); externally, 0.62 at Massachusetts General Hospital (n=424, 375 with complete data, JCO 2005) against 0.59 for AJCC stage, p=0.004; 0.61 in a second independent cohort (Br J Surg 2009)
Runs on EHR data?: Partly, needs pathology, imaging or a send-out assay. Fourteen operative and pathology fields, including margin status, splenectomy and portal vein resection. All in an operative note; few are structured.
Developed on: Memorial Sloan Kettering pancreatic resection series
Reference: Brennan, M. F., Kattan, M. W., Klimstra, D., & Conlon, K. (2004). Prognostic nomogram for patients undergoing resection for adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. Annals of Surgery, 240(2), 293-8. https://doi.org/10.1097/01.sla.0000133125.85489.07
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form. Coefficients from ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/PancreaticCancer1YrSurvivalAfterResectionforAdenocarcinoma.
How it was verified: Route 1, CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R: the reference script copies the model expression VERBATIM from riskcalc.org's server.R and runs it under R 4.6.1, so the comparison is against their arithmetic rather than our reading of it
Where the equation came from: Coefficients from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/PancreaticCancer1YrSurvivalAfterResectionforAdenocarcinoma, which riskcalc.org's own page cites to the publication above.
Citation: Brennan MF, Kattan MW, Klimstra D, Conlon K. Ann Surg. 2004;240(2)
Scope / caveats: After resection for adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. Validated ranges enforced: age 33-89, positive nodes 0-39, negative nodes 0-83, size 0.1-16 cm.

Question: Prediction
Model: ERSPC RC3 (DRE-volume, biopsy-naïve)
Architecture detail: Multivariable logistic regression: weighted sum of 3 predictors (log2 PSA, log2 prostate volume, DRE) pushed through a logistic link to a probability.
Core formula:
logit(p) = −1.826
           + 1.024 · (log₂ PSA − 2.0)
           − 1.500 · (log₂ volume_class − 5.4)
           + 0.992 · DRE
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUC 0.61–0.77 across validation cohorts
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. PSA, prostate volume and the DRE finding.
Developed on: not recorded yet
Reference: Roobol, M. J., Schröder, F. H., Hugosson, J., Jones, J. S., Kattan, M. W., Klein, E. A., Hamdy, F., Neal, D., Donovan, J., Parekh, D. J., Ankerst, D., Bartsch, G., Klocker, H., Horninger, W., Benchikh, A., Salama, G., Villers, A., Freedland, S. J., Moreira, D. M., . . . Steyerberg, E. W. (2012). Importance of prostate volume in the European Randomised Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer (ERSPC) risk calculators: results from the prostate biopsy collaborative group. World Journal of Urology, 30(2), 149-55. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00345-011-0804-y
Where the equation sits: Appendix, under the heading 'Formulas used to calculate volume classes and the DRE ERSPC RC risks'. Printed there as lpDRE_ERSPC_riskcalc = -1.826 + 1.024 x (log2(PSA) - 2.0) - 1.50 x (log2(volumeclasses) - 5.4) + 0.992 x DRE, which matches this library's coefficients term for term.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 by extracting the coefficients from SWOP's own Flash calculator (/2011/swf/c03dre.swf)
Where the equation came from: Roobol/PBCG World J Urol 2012 appendix; PMC3321270
Citation: Roobol MJ et al. World J Urol. 2012;30(2):149-155. PMC3321270

Question: Prediction
Model: Extended PBCG (high-grade prostate cancer on biopsy, 1,024 sub-models)
Architecture detail: Binary logistic regression for high-grade disease, fitted 1,024 times, once for every pattern of the ten optional predictors. The pattern selects the sub-model; nothing is imputed.
Core formula:
p(high grade) = 1 / (1 + e^(−Xβ))

  Xβ   from one of 1,024 fitted sub-models
  the sub-model is chosen by WHICH of the ten optional
  predictors were supplied, not by imputing the rest
  PSA and prostate volume enter as log₂
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUC 75.7 (95% CI 74.4-77.1) in external validation, against 66.9 (65.4-68.5) for the 2018 PBCG on the SAME validation set; internal cross-validation median 80, range 74-84
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. Requires only age and PSA. The other ten predictors are optional, and each pattern of them has its own fitted sub-model, 1,024 in all, so a record missing family history is scored by the model fitted without it rather than by imputing one. This is the design an EHR deployment wants.
Developed on: Prostate Biopsy Collaborative Group: up to 12,703 biopsies across ten international cohorts, with the full 12-factor model fitted on 1,334 biopsies from three cohorts
Reference: Neumair, M., Kattan, M. W., Freedland, S. J., Haese, A., Guerrios-Rivera, L., De Hoedt, A. M., Liss, M. A., Leach, R. J., Boorjian, S. A., Cooperberg, M. R., Poyet, C., Saba, K., Herkommer, K., Meissner, V. H., Vickers, A. J., & Ankerst, D. P. (2022). Accommodating heterogeneous missing data patterns for prostate cancer risk prediction. BMC Medical Research Methodology, 22(1), 200. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12874-022-01674-x
Where the equation sits: Additional file 2 (12874_2022_1674_MOESM2_ESM.txt), the full coefficient matrix and risk() function. Table 3 of the main text prints odds ratios for the full, standard and minimal models, which is what the main text carries.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-07, route 1, against the authors' OWN published R rather than a vendor deployment, the strongest provenance in this library
Where the equation came from: Additional file 2 of the article itself (CC BY 4.0), the complete 1,024 x 13 coefficient matrix and the risk() function, published as journal supplementary material rather than taken from a deployment.
Citation: Neumair M, Kattan MW, Freedland SJ, et al. Accommodating heterogeneous missing data patterns for prostate cancer risk prediction. BMC Med Res Methodol. 2022;22(1):200
Scope / caveats: Prostate Biopsy Collaborative Group, ten international cohorts of men referred for biopsy. Predicts HIGH-GRADE disease only (Gleason grade group >= 2); it does not report risk of any cancer, which the 2018 predecessor did. Age and PSA are mandatory. The 2018 version was found on external validation to over-predict in Black and other groups; that has not been re-tested here for this version. CAUTION, measured across all 1,024 sub-models: the African-ancestry coefficient CHANGES SIGN depending on which optional fields are supplied. It is protective in 412 sub-models and harmful in 100. OR 0.68 in the full 12-factor model (1,334 biopsies, p=0.08) against OR 1.26 in the six-factor one (8,432 biopsies, p=0.0005). Which sub-model a patient lands in is decided by what the caller happened to fill in, so supplying MORE data can move this term from harmful to protective. Do not read the term as a population effect.

Question: Prediction
Model: PBCG (Prostate Biopsy Collaborative Group; no cancer / low grade / high grade)
Architecture detail: Multinomial logistic regression over three outcomes (no cancer, Gleason 6, Gleason 7+), with eight fitted coefficient sets so a record missing prior biopsy, DRE or family history uses the model fitted without it rather than an imputed value.
Core formula:
S₁ = β_low · x        S₂ = β_high · x

  P(no cancer)  = 1 / (1 + e^S₁ + e^S₂)
  P(low grade)  = e^S₁ / (1 + e^S₁ + e^S₂)
  P(high grade) = e^S₂ / (1 + e^S₁ + e^S₂)

  x = [1, log₂PSA, age, African ancestry, + known optionals]
  one of 8 coefficient sets, by which optionals are known
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUC 75.5% internal validation, 72.3% external (vs 72.3%/69.7% for PCPTRC 2.0)
Runs on EHR data?: Yes, routine EHR fields. Age, PSA and DRE are routine at the point a biopsy is being considered, and prior-biopsy status is in the record whenever there was one. African ancestry and family history are the two that are inconsistently coded, and the model does not require them: there are eight fitted sub-models, one per pattern of missing prior-biopsy / DRE / family-history data, so a record missing those is scored by the sub-model fitted without them rather than by imputation.
Developed on: 15,611 men undergoing 16,369 biopsies at eight North American institutions 2006-2017; validated at three European institutions
Reference: Ankerst, D. P., Straubinger, J., Selig, K., Guerrios, L., De Hoedt, A., Hernandez, J., Liss, M. A., Leach, R. J., Freedland, S. J., Kattan, M. W., Nam, R., Haese, A., Montorsi, F., Boorjian, S. A., Cooperberg, M. R., Poyet, C., Vertosick, E., & Vickers, A. J. (2018). A Contemporary Prostate Biopsy Risk Calculator Based on Multiple Heterogeneous Cohorts. European Urology, 74(2), 197-203. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eururo.2018.05.003
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form. The coefficients are in the deployed calculator's R source, ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/PBCG, as eight coefficient sets (one per missing-data pattern). Establishing this by parity against that source is what verified the model.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R, route 1
Where the equation came from: Coefficients from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/PBCG. Multinomial logistic with 'no cancer' as the reference outcome, and EIGHT coefficient sets, one per pattern of missing prior-biopsy / DRE / family-history data.
Citation: Ankerst DP, Straubinger J, Selig K, et al. Eur Urol. 2018;74(2):197-203
Scope / caveats: Men undergoing prostate biopsy. Predicts high-grade (Gleason 7+) separately from any cancer, which is the actionable question. NOT strictly better than ERSPC RC3: external validation found PBCG improved calibration in White men but OVER-PREDICTED in Black and other groups at most thresholds, so both are kept.

Question: Response
Model: Dutasteride chemoprevention (9 outcomes x 2 arms, benefit and harm)
Architecture detail: Seventeen Cox sub-models: nine outcomes each predicted on and off dutasteride, with restricted cubic splines and per-outcome applicability bounds, so the reported quantity is the treated-minus-untreated difference rather than either risk.
Core formula:
risk = 1 − S₀^exp(score)        per outcome, per arm

  difference = on-drug − off-drug
               negative is benefit, positive is harm
  9 outcomes × 2 arms (ASAP has only the on-drug arm)
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Concordance index by outcome, placebo/dutasteride: high-grade PCa 0.69/0.71, BPH symptoms 0.70/0.60, acute urinary retention 0.66/0.62, any PCa 0.62/0.61, erectile dysfunction 0.59/0.60, UTI 0.55/0.51, HGPIN 0.53/0.47, gynecomastia 0.52/0.52, ASAP 0.48/0.53. Four of the nine are at or below chance in at least one arm and the paper says so
Runs on EHR data?: No, needs questionnaire or patient-reported items. Sexual activity, history of impotence and of libido problems, IPSS symptom score, maximum urinary flow and post-void residual volume. Urology questionnaires and urodynamics, not routine records.
Developed on: REDUCE trial: men with a prior negative 6- to 12-core prostate biopsy
Reference: Nguyen, C. T., Isariyawongse, B., Yu, C., & Kattan, M. W. (2012). The REDUCE metagram: a comprehensive prediction tool for determining the utility of dutasteride chemoprevention in men at risk for prostate cancer. Frontiers in Oncology, 2, 138. https://doi.org/10.3389/fonc.2012.00138
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form. 315 coefficients across 17 Cox sub-models, machine-extracted from ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/ProstateCancerConsideringDutasteride by tests/parity/reference/dutasteride_extract.py.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R, route 1
Where the equation came from: Coefficients machine-extracted from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/ProstateCancerConsideringDutasteride by tests/parity/reference/dutasteride_extract.py. 17 Cox sub-models (9 outcomes x 2 arms, minus one missing arm), 315 coefficients, each risk = 1 - S0^exp(score) with its own predictor subset, spline knots and applicability bounds.
Citation: Nguyen CT, Isariyawongse B, Yu C, Kattan MW, models for men with a prior negative biopsy considering dutasteride (REDUCE)
Scope / caveats: Men with a prior negative 6- to 12-core biopsy in the past 6 months (REDUCE). Nine outcomes, three of them harms (erectile dysfunction, gynecomastia, urinary tract infection). It reproduces REDUCE's central finding that dutasteride LOWERS overall prostate cancer but RAISES high-grade disease, a model reporting only the overall reduction would answer half the question. Applicability bounds differ per outcome, so a patient can be answerable for some outcomes and not others; unanswerable ones return None rather than a guess.

Question: Prognosis
Model: UCSF-CAPRA (preoperative recurrence risk)
Architecture detail: Additive integer point score (0-10) distilled from a Cox model; at prediction time it is table lookup and addition, with no regression evaluated.
Core formula:
total = PSA + Gleason + T-stage + %positive-cores + age   (0–10)

  PSA      2.1–6 → 0, 6.1–10 → 1, 10.1–20 → 2, 20.1–30 → 3, >30 → 4
  Gleason  0, 1 or 3, there is no 2-point level
  0–2 low · 3–5 intermediate · 6–10 high
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Concordance index 0.66
Runs on EHR data?: Partly, needs pathology, imaging or a send-out assay. PSA and age are routine; Gleason grades, T stage and percent positive cores come from the pathology report.
Developed on: not recorded yet
Reference: Cooperberg, M. R., Pasta, D. J., Elkin, E. P., Litwin, M. S., Latini, D. M., Du Chane, J., & Carroll, P. R. (2005). The University of California, San Francisco Cancer of the Prostate Risk Assessment score: a straightforward and reliable preoperative predictor of disease recurrence after radical prostatectomy. The Journal of Urology, 173(6), 1938-42. https://doi.org/10.1097/01.ju.0000158155.33890.e7
Where the equation sits: Table 1, 'The UCSF-CAPRA scoring system'. Described in Methods under 'Development of the UCSF Cancer of the Prostate Risk Assessment (UCSF-CAPRA)'. The printed points match this library: PSA 0-4, Gleason 0/1/3 (no 2-point level), T stage 0-1, percent positive biopsies 0-1 at the 34% threshold, age 0-1 at 50.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against MDCalc's published point schema, entry by entry across all five fields (PSA 5 bands, Gleason 0/1/3 with no 2-point level, T-stage, percent cores, age)
Where the equation came from: J Urol 2005;173(6):1938-1942, PMC2948569 Table 1. PSA 0-4, Gleason 0/1/3, T-stage 0-1, percent positive cores 0-1, age 0-1; total 0-10
Citation: Cooperberg MR et al. J Urol. 2005;173(6):1938-1942
Scope / caveats: preoperative CAPRA only; CAPRA-S (postoperative, Cancer 2011) not implemented. The 0-2/3-5/6-10 risk banding this returns is a downstream convention and is NOT defined in Cooperberg 2005, which groups scores as 0-1/2/3/4/5/6/>=7 (Table 4); only the point table is that paper's Table 1. The paper does publish score-to-outcome tables (Tables 3-4) which this library has not transcribed, which is why `risk` is None.
